t.E332.agn: JECFA included potassium citrates in the citric acid group ADI ('not limited'); it noted that potassium citrate has been used in medicine for many years at doses of up to 10 g per day.
t.E332.body: Citric acid and citrates are normal intermediates of the tricarboxylic acid (Krebs) cycle, which produces energy in the body.
t.E332.found.0: May be used in many foods in the EU at quantum satis (as much as needed)
t.E332.found.1: Infant formulae and complementary foods for infants (in the EU only under limited conditions such as pH adjustment)
t.E332.prod: Obtained by neutralising citric acid with potassium hydroxide or potassium carbonate.
t.E332.regx.0: ADI 'not limited'; included in the citric acid group ADI.
t.E332.regx.1: Group I additive; generally permitted at quantum satis (as much as needed).
t.E332.regx.2: Permitted under limited conditions in infant formulae and complementary foods for infants.
t.E332.summary: The potassium salts of citric acid. Used as acidity regulators in drinks and desserts.
t.E332.what: The potassium salts of citric acid, used as acidity regulators, buffers and stabilisers.
